message:
Stiffening the 40 m span out of the walking band is disproportionate, so pure added damping is preferred over added steel. In plain words the deck would need much more steel to move frequency enough to matter. Moving first mode from 1.9 Hz to 2.3 Hz needs 46.5 percent more bending stiffness from the stiffness-increase calculation (E27), and to 2.5 Hz needs 73.1 percent more from the higher-target calculation (E28), while 1.9 Hz sits inside the 1.25 to 2.3 Hz critical vertical range reported in the Human-Induced Vibration on Lightweight Footbridges — 2024 (E19) and the comfort-class review in the Microsoft Word - IJLCPE010105 VENUTI_no downsample.doc (E18). This matches the finding in the Pedestrian Bridge Dynamics: Footfall-Induced Vibration and Damping (E22) that the most direct fix once a resonance-sensitive frequency is identified is usually to add damping rather than to redesign the whole structure, and the finding in the Keep to the beat: The Physics of Spontaneous Synchronization (E23) that increasing stiffness was considered impractical because it required major structural additions, significant added mass, aesthetic impact and high cost.

Added hardware must stay a small fraction of live load and must clamp to the girders without welding to avoid fatigue details. In plain words the Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), weighs about ten people against hundreds of people of crowd load. The TMD static weight is 7.85 kN from the static-weight calculation (E26), against a 600 kN total pedestrian live load for a 3 m wide deck from the live-load estimate (E30), which is about 1.31 percent and meets the assumed 2 percent rule. The 5.0 kN per m2 crowd load basis is taken from the Bison Pedestrian Bridge  - Bridge  | Built By Bison Ltd | BIM Library (E20) tested to 5.0 kN per m2 and the Bridge Design| Bridge loading idealisation for grillage analysis for eurocode loading. (E21) stating the pedestrian live load shall be taken as 5.0 kN per m2. Clamped preloaded High-Strength Friction-Grip, defined as High-Strength Friction-Grip (HSFG), bolts are used because the Load‐deformation behavior of injection bolts for maintenance of steel structures under dynamic loads (E24) regulates fatigue of preloaded bolts by detail category in EN 1993-1-9 and the Loss of preload in pretensioned bolts - TU Delft - [PDF Document] (E25) shows bolt relaxation can reduce fatigue life through loss of clamp load, so friction clamp without welds is the buildable load path.

Damper and stop reactions are small against live load but cycle at footfall frequency, so they still need a continuous path into the main girders at midspan. In plain words the peak push-pull per unit is only a few people of weight cycling at 1.9 Hz. Peak TMD dynamic force at the simulated stroke is 5.22 kN from the dynamic-force calculation (E29), about seven body weights, so each bracket plus stop must carry roughly 13.1 kN static plus dynamic into the girders, which is tiny against 600 kN crowd load but governs for loosening and fatigue, not ultimate strength. My position is not ready, because pier and abutment checks for these midspan reactions and the clamping procedure still need agreement.
